And the Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd told us, al-A'mash told us, on the authority of Abu Khalid, on the authority of Wahb al-Suwa'i, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I and the Hour have been sent like this, one is about to overtake the other," and al-A'mash joined the index and middle fingers. [[Al-Musnad (4/309).]]

And the Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Mughirah told us, al-Awza'i told us, Isma'il ibn 'Ubayd Allah told us, who said: Anas ibn Malik came to al-Walid ibn 'Abd al-Malik, and he asked him: "What did you hear from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that mentions the Hour?" He said: "I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'You and the Hour are like these two.'" [[Al-Musnad (3/223).]] Ahmad alone narrated it, may Allah have mercy on him. There is also corroboration for this in the Sahih, in the names of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): that he is al-Hashir (the Gatherer), at whose feet people will be gathered. [[Ibn Kathir's note: the reference is to the Sahih collections.]]

And the Imam Ahmad said: Bahz ibn Asad told us, Sulayman ibn al-Mughirah told us, Humayd ibn Hilal told us, on the authority of Khalid ibn 'Umayr, who said: 'Utbah ibn Ghazwan delivered a sermon, (Bahz said: he had said this before this time): "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) addressed us, and he praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: 'To proceed: this world has announced its departure and has turned away swiftly, and there remains of it only a small residue like the residue of a vessel, which its owner drains. You are moving from it to an abode that has no end, so move on with the best that is in your presence. It has been mentioned to us that a stone is thrown from the brink of Hell and it falls into it for seventy years without reaching its bottom. By Allah, it will be filled! Are you astonished? By Allah, it has been mentioned to us that the distance between the two leaves of the gate of Paradise is forty years' journey, and a day will come upon it when it will be crowded to capacity.'" And he mentioned the rest of the hadith. Muslim alone narrated it. [[Al-Musnad (4/174) and Sahih Muslim no. (2967).]]

Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub told me, Ibn 'Ulayyah told me, 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed us, on the authority of Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, who said: "We stayed in al-Mada'in, and we were a farsakh (league) away from it. Then Friday came, my father attended and I attended with him, and Hudhayfah gave us a sermon. He said: 'Indeed Allah says: ﴿The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split﴾. Indeed the Hour has drawn near, and indeed the moon has split. Indeed the world has announced its parting. Indeed today is the training ground, and tomorrow is the race.' I said to my father: 'Will people race tomorrow?' He said: 'O my son, you are truly ignorant. It is only the race of deeds.'"

Then the next Friday came, and we attended, and Hudhayfah gave the sermon. He said: "Indeed Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, says: ﴿The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split﴾. Indeed the world has announced its parting. Indeed today is the training ground and tomorrow is the race. Indeed the goal is the Fire, and the foremost is the one who precedes to Paradise." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (27/51).]]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and the moon has split﴾: this happened during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), as is established by the widely transmitted hadiths with sound chains of narration. It is also established in the Sahih on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "Five have passed: the Romans, the smoke, the grasp (al-lizam), the great assault (al-batshah), and the moon." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4767).]] This is an agreed matter among the scholars: that the splitting of the moon occurred during the time of the Prophet (ﷺ), and that it was one of the magnificent miracles.

Mention of the hadiths related on this:

The narration of Anas ibn Malik:

The Imam Ahmad said: 'Abd al-Razzaq told us, Ma'mar told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, who said: "The people of Makkah asked the Prophet (ﷺ) for a sign, so the moon split in Makkah twice." Then he (the Prophet) recited: ﴿The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split﴾.

Muslim also narrated it on the authority of Muhammad ibn Rafi', on the authority of 'Abd al-Razzaq. [[Al-Musnad (3/165) and Sahih Muslim no. (2802).]]

Al-Bukhari said: 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abd al-Wahhab told me, Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal told us, Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, that the people of Makkah asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to show them a sign, so he showed them the moon split into two halves, until they saw Hira between them. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3868).]]

Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) also narrated it through the hadith of Yunus ibn Muhammad al-Mu'addib, on the authority of Shaybān, on the authority of Qatadah. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4867) and Sahih Muslim no. (2802).]] Muslim also narrated it through the hadith of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi and Yahya al-Qattan and others, on the authority of Shu'bah, on the authority of Qatadah, with the same. [[Sahih Muslim no. (2802); al-Bukhari also narrated it in his Sahih no. (4868) through the route of Yahya on the authority of Shu'bah.]]

The narration of Jubayr ibn Mut'im, may Allah be pleased with him:

The Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Kathir told us, Sulayman ibn Kathir told us, on the authority of Husayn ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, on the authority of his father, who said: "The moon split during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and became two halves: one half on this mountain and one half on that mountain. They said: 'Muhammad has bewitched us.' Then they said: 'If he has bewitched us, he cannot bewitch all the people.'"

Al-Imam Ahmad alone narrated it through this route. Al-Bayhaqi traced it in *al-Dala'il* through the route of Muhammad ibn Kathir, on the authority of his brother Sulayman ibn Kathir, on the authority of Husayn ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, [with him] [[Addition from M.]]. [[Al-Musnad (4/81) and Dala'il al-Nubuwwah of al-Bayhaqi (2/268).]] Ibn Jarir narrated it in the same way through the hadith of Muhammad ibn Fudayl and others, on the authority of Husayn, with it. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (27/51).]] Al-Bayhaqi also narrated it through the route of Ibrahim ibn Tahman and Hushaym, both on the authority of Husayn, on the authority of Jubayr ibn Muhammad ibn Jubayr ibn Mut'im, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, and mentioned it. [[Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (2/268).]]

The narration of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Abbas [may Allah be pleased with them both] [[Addition from M.]]:

Al-Bukhari said: Yahya ibn Bukayr told us, Bakr told us, on the authority of Ja'far, on the authority of 'Iraq ibn Malik, on the authority of 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Abd Allah ibn 'Utbah, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The moon split during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4866).]]

Al-Bukhari and Muslim also narrated it through the hadith of Bakr ibn Mudar, on the authority of Ja'far ibn Rabi'ah, on the authority of 'Iraq [ibn Malik] [[Addition from A.]], with the like of it. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (3638) and Sahih Muslim no. (2803).]]

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Muthanna told us, 'Abd al-A'la told us, Dawud ibn Abi Hind told us, on the authority of 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split. And if they see a sign, they turn away and say: "Continuous magic."﴾ He said: "That has already passed. It was before the Hijrah. The moon split until they saw its two halves."

Al-'Awfi also narrated something similar from Ibn 'Abbas.

And al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn 'Amr al-Bazzar told us, Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Qut'i told us, Muhammad ibn Bakr told us, Ibn Jurayj told us, on the authority of 'Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of 'Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The moon was eclipsed during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they said: 'The moon has been bewitched.' Then this was revealed: ﴿The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split﴾ up to His saying: ﴿continuous﴾."

The narration of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar:

The Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bayhaqi said: Abu 'Abd Allah al-Hafiz and Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qadi informed us, both saying: Abu al-'Abbas al-Asamm told us, al-'Abbas ibn Muhammad al-Duri told us, Wahb ibn Jarir told us, on the authority of Shu'bah, on the authority of al-A'mash, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, regarding His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿The Hour has drawn near and the moon has split﴾, he said: "This happened during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): it split into two halves, one half beyond the mountain and one half behind the mountain. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'O Allah, bear witness.'"

Muslim and al-Tirmidhi also narrated it in this way through various routes, on the authority of Shu'bah, on the authority of al-A'mash, on the authority of Mujahid, with it. [[Dala'il al-Nubuwwah (2/267), Sahih Muslim no. (2801) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3288).]] Muslim said: like the narration of Mujahid on the authority of Abu Ma'mar, on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih" (good and sound).

The narration of 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud:

The Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Najih, on the authority of Mujahid, on the authority of Abu Ma'mar, on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "The moon split into two halves during the time of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), until they looked at it, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Bear witness.'"

Al-Bukhari and Muslim also narrated it in this way through the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah, with it. [[Al-Musnad (1/377), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4865) and Sahih Muslim no. (2800).]] Both of them also narrated it through the hadith of al-A'mash, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Abu Ma'mar 'Abd Allah ibn Sakhbarah, on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud, with it. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4864) and Sahih Muslim no. (2800).]]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 54, verse 1–5 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn Jarir said: Isa ibn Uthman ibn Isa al-Ramli narrated to me, saying: My paternal uncle Yahya ibn Isa narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from a man, from Abdullah, who said: "We were with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at Mina when the moon split, and a group took (to the road) behind the mountain. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Bear witness, bear witness.'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (27/50).]]

Al-Bukhari said: Abu al-Duha also narrated, from Masruq, from Abdullah: "in Makkah." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (295).]]

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Abu Awana narrated to us, from al-Mughira, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The moon split during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Quraysh said: "This is the sorcery of Ibn Abi Kabsha." He said: They said: "Look at what the travellers (al-saffar) will bring you, for Muhammad cannot bewitch all the people." He said: The travellers came, and they said: "That is so." [[Musnad al-Tayalisi, no. (295).]]

Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah al-Hafiz informed us, Abu al-Abbas Muhammad ibn Ya'qub informed us, al-Abbas ibn Muhammad al-Duri narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Hushaym narrated to us, al-Mughira narrated to us, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from Abdullah, who said: The moon split in Makkah until it became two halves. The disbelievers of Quraysh, the people of Makkah, said: "This is sorcery which Ibn Abi Kabsha has worked upon you. Look at the travellers: if they saw what you saw, then he has spoken the truth; but if they did not see the like of what you saw, then it is sorcery with which he has bewitched you." He said: The travellers were asked, and they came from every direction, and they said: "We saw it."

Ibn Jarir narrated it through the hadith of al-Mughira, with this chain. [[Dala'il al-Nubuwwa of al-Bayhaqi (2/266) and Tafsir al-Tabari (27/50).]] He added: Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split﴾. Then Ibn Jarir said: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to me, saying: Ibn Ulayya narrated to us, Ayyub informed us, from Muhammad (that is, Ibn Sirin), who said: "I was told that Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, used to say: 'The moon indeed split.'" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (27/51).]]

Ibn Jarir also said: Muhammad ibn Imara narrated to me, Amr ibn Hammad narrated to us, Asbat narrated to us, from Simak, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from Abdullah, who said: "I indeed saw the mountain through the split of the moon when it split."

Imam Ahmad narrated it from Mu'ammal, from Isra'il, from Simak, from Ibrahim, from al-Aswad, from Abdullah, who said: The moon split during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), until I saw the mountain between the two halves of the moon. [[Al-Musnad (1/413).]]

Layth said, from Mujahid: The moon split during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and became two halves, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Abu Bakr: "Bear witness, O Abu Bakr." The polytheists said: "The moon has been bewitched until it split." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (27/51).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿And if they see a sign﴾, meaning: a proof, a clear argument and a demonstration, ﴿they turn away﴾, meaning: they do not submit to it, but turn away from it and leave it behind their backs, ﴿and say: "Continuous magic."﴾, meaning: they say: "This which we have witnessed of proofs is magic with which we have been bewitched."

The meaning of ﴿mustamirr﴾ is: passing away. This was said by Mujahid, Qatada and others, meaning: false and vanishing, having no permanence.

﴿And they denied and followed their desires﴾, meaning: they denied the truth when it came to them, and followed what their opinions and desires commanded them, out of their ignorance and feeble intellect.

* *

His saying: ﴿And every matter will be settled﴾. Qatada said: Its meaning is that good befalls the people of good, and evil befalls the people of evil.

Ibn Jurayj said: ﴿mustaqirr﴾, meaning it will settle upon its people. Mujahid said: ﴿And every matter will be settled﴾ means on the Day of Resurrection.

Al-Suddi said: ﴿mustaqirr﴾ means: it will occur.

* *

His saying: ﴿And there has certainly come to them of the news﴾, meaning: of the reports about the stories of the nations who denied the messengers, and what punishment, retribution and torment befell them, which is recited to them in this Qur'an, ﴿that which contains a deterrent﴾, meaning: that which contains an admonition for them against polytheism and persistence in denial.

* *

His saying: ﴿Perfect wisdom﴾, meaning: in His guidance of whom He guides and His leading astray of whom He leads astray. ﴿But warnings avail not﴾, meaning: what use are warnings to one for whom Allah has decreed wretchedness and set a seal upon his heart? Who then can guide him after Allah? This verse is like His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Say: "To Allah belongs the conclusive proof; had He willed, He would have guided you all."﴾ [al-An'am: 149], and likewise His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And signs and warnings avail not a people who do not believe﴾ [Yunus: 101].

Allah says: So turn away, O Muhammad, from those who, when they see a sign, turn away and say, "This is continuous magic." Leave them alone and wait for them. ﴿On the Day when the Caller calls to a terrible thing﴾, meaning to a dreadful, frightful matter, which is the station of reckoning and the afflictions in it, along with the earthquakes and terrors. ﴿With eyes humbled﴾, meaning their eyes will be abased. ﴿They will emerge from the graves﴾, the graves being the tombs. ﴿As if they were locusts dispersed﴾, meaning that in their dispersal and the speed of their movement toward the station of reckoning, in answer to the Caller, they are like locusts scattered across the horizons. For this reason He said: ﴿Hastening toward the Caller﴾, meaning hurrying ﴿toward the Caller﴾, neither deviating nor lagging behind. ﴿The disbelievers will say, "This is a difficult day."﴾, meaning a day of intense terror, grim and severe. ﴿So that Day will be a difficult day, not easy for the disbelievers﴾ [Al-Muddaththir: 9, 10].

Allah says: So turn away, O Muhammad, from those who, when they see a sign, turn away and say, "This is continuous magic." Leave them alone and wait for them. ﴿On the Day when the Caller calls to a terrible thing﴾, meaning to a dreadful, frightful matter, which is the station of reckoning and the afflictions in it, along with the earthquakes and terrors. ﴿With eyes humbled﴾, meaning their eyes will be abased. ﴿They will emerge from the graves﴾, the graves being the tombs. ﴿As if they were locusts dispersed﴾, meaning that in their dispersal and the speed of their movement toward the station of reckoning, in answer to the Caller, they are like locusts scattered across the horizons. For this reason He said: ﴿Hastening toward the Caller﴾, meaning hurrying ﴿toward the Caller﴾, neither deviating nor lagging behind. ﴿The disbelievers will say, "This is a difficult day."﴾, meaning a day of intense terror, grim and severe. ﴿So that Day will be a difficult day, not easy for the disbelievers﴾ [Al-Muddaththir: 9, 10].

Allah says: So turn away, O Muhammad, from those who, when they see a sign, turn away and say, "This is continuous magic." Leave them alone and wait for them. ﴿On the Day when the Caller calls to a terrible thing﴾, meaning to a dreadful, frightful matter, which is the station of reckoning and the afflictions in it, along with the earthquakes and terrors. ﴿With eyes humbled﴾, meaning their eyes will be abased. ﴿They will emerge from the graves﴾, the graves being the tombs. ﴿As if they were locusts dispersed﴾, meaning that in their dispersal and the speed of their movement toward the station of reckoning, in answer to the Caller, they are like locusts scattered across the horizons. For this reason He said: ﴿Hastening toward the Caller﴾, meaning hurrying ﴿toward the Caller﴾, neither deviating nor lagging behind. ﴿The disbelievers will say, "This is a difficult day."﴾, meaning a day of intense terror, grim and severe. ﴿So that Day will be a difficult day, not easy for the disbelievers﴾ [Al-Muddaththir: 9, 10].

Allah the Exalted says: "The people of Noah denied before your people, O Muhammad. They denied Our servant and said, 'He is a madman,' and he was rebuked." That is, they openly declared him a liar and accused him of being possessed.

Mujahid said regarding "and he was rebuked": it means he was driven mad (istuṭīra junūnan). It was also said that "and he was rebuked" means they scolded him, drove him away and threatened him: "If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be among those stoned" [ash-Shu'ara': 116]. This was said by Ibn Zayd, and this interpretation is sound and well-directed.

"So he called upon his Lord: 'I am overpowered, so help [me]'" — that is, I am too weak against these people and unable to resist them, "so help [me]," i.e., You support Your religion.

Allah the Exalted said: "So We opened the gates of heaven with water pouring down." As-Suddi said: it is abundant. "And We caused the earth to burst forth with springs," meaning every part of the earth gushed forth, even the ovens, which are the places of fire, gushed forth as springs. "And the waters met for a matter already decreed," that is, the water from the sky and the water from the earth met in a matter that had been decreed.

Ibn Jurayj reported from Ibn Abbas: "So We opened the gates of heaven with water pouring down" — abundant. The sky had not rained before that day, nor after it, and not from clouds. The gates of heaven were opened with water without clouds that day, "and the waters met for a matter already decreed."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated that Ibn al-Kawwa asked Ali about the Milky Way, and he said: "It is the crack of the sky, and from it the sky was opened with pouring water."

"And We carried him upon [a vessel] of planks and nails": Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Qurazi, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd said: these are the nails. Ibn Jarir chose this view and said: its singular is disar, and it is also said dasir, as one says habik and hibak, the plural being hubuk.

Mujahid said: ad-dusur are the ribs of the ship. Ikrimah and al-Hasan said: it is its breast, which the waves strike. Ad-Dahhak said: ad-dusur are its sides and its base. Al-Awfi reported from Ibn Abbas: it is its keel.

* *

Allah's saying: "Sailing under Our eyes" — that is, by Our command, in Our sight, and under Our protection and care, "as a reward for one who had been denied" — that is, a reward for them for their disbelief in Allah, and as a vindication of Noah, peace be upon him.

* *

Allah's saying: "And We have left it as a sign." Qatadah said: Allah preserved Noah's ship until the first of this Ummah reached it. Apparently what is meant by this is the category of ships, as in His saying: "And a sign for them is that We carried their offspring in the laden ship, and We created for them of its like that which they ride" [Ya-Sin: 41-42], and He said: "Indeed, when the water rose high, We carried you in the sailing ship, that We might make it for you a reminder and that an attentive ear would retain it" [al-Haqqah: 11-12]. Therefore He said here: "So is there any who will remember?" — that is, is there anyone who will be mindful and take heed?

Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Aswad, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited to me "fa-hal min muddakir" and a man said: "O Abu Abd ar-Rahman, is it muddakir or muddakir?" He said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited to me "muddakir" [[Al-Musnad (1/395).]]

Thus al-Bukhari also narrated: Yahya narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Isra'il, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Aswad [[In M: "from Abu al-Aswad".]] ibn Yazid, from Abd Allah who said: I recited to the Prophet (ﷺ) "fa-hal min muddakir" and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "fa-hal min muddakir" [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4874).]]

Al-Bukhari also narrated from the hadith of Shu'bah, from Abu Ishaq, from al-Aswad, from Abd Allah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to recite: "fa-hal min muddakir" [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4869).]].

He also said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, from Abu Ishaq, that he heard a man asking al-Aswad: "fa-hal min muddakir" or "muddakir"? He said: I heard Abd Allah reciting "fa-hal min muddakir," and he said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) reciting it "fa-hal min muddakir" with a dal.

Muslim narrated this hadith, and the authors of the Sunan except Ibn Majah, from the hadith of Abu Ishaq [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (4871), Sahih Muslim no. (823), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3994), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2937), Sunan an-Nasa'i (2/150).]].

* *

Allah's saying: "So how was My punishment and My warning?" — that is, how was My punishment upon those who disbelieved in Me, denied My messengers, and did not heed what My warnings brought, and how did I avenge them and take retribution on their behalf.

"And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance" — that is, We made its recitation easy and made its meaning accessible to whoever wishes it, so that people may remember. As He said: "A Book which We have revealed to you, blessed, that they might ponder its verses and that those of understanding might be reminded" [Sad: 29], and Allah the Exalted said: "So We have only made it easy in your tongue that you may give good tidings thereby to the righteous and warn thereby a people contentious" [Maryam: 97].

Mujahid said: "And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance" means: We made its recitation simple.

As-Suddi said: We made its recitation easy upon the tongues.

Ad-Dahhak reported from Ibn Abbas: Were it not that Allah made it easy upon the tongues of human beings, no one among creation would have been able to speak the speech of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

I say: Among the ease Allah, the Exalted, has granted people in reciting the Qur'an is what was mentioned earlier from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Indeed this Qur'an was revealed in seven ahruf (modes/dialects)." We have cited the hadith with its chains and wordings in a way that makes repeating it here unnecessary, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

* *

Allah's saying: "So is there any who will remember?" — that is, is there anyone who will be mindful through this Qur'an whose memorization and meaning Allah has made easy?

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: Is there anyone who will refrain from sins?

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn Rafi' narrated to us, Damrah [[In A: "Hamzah".]] narrated to us, from Ibn Shawdhab, from Mutar — he is al-Warraq — regarding Allah's saying: "So is there any who will remember?": Is there anyone seeking knowledge so that he may be helped in it?

Likewise al-Bukhari recorded it in a categorical form from Mutar al-Warraq, and [thus] it was narrated by Ibn Jarir [[Tafsir al-Tabari (27/57).]]. And it is reported from Qatadah something similar.

Allah the Exalted says: "The people of Noah denied before your people, O Muhammad. They denied Our servant and said, 'He is a madman,' and he was rebuked." That is, they openly declared him a liar and accused him of being possessed.

Mujahid said regarding "and he was rebuked": it means he was driven mad (istuṭīra junūnan). It was also said that "and he was rebuked" means they scolded him, drove him away and threatened him: "If you do not desist, O Noah, you will surely be among those stoned" [ash-Shu'ara': 116]. This was said by Ibn Zayd, and this interpretation is sound and well-directed.

"So he called upon his Lord: 'I am overpowered, so help [me]'" — that is, I am too weak against these people and unable to resist them, "so help [me]," i.e., You support Your religion.

Allah the Exalted said: "So We opened the gates of heaven with water pouring down." As-Suddi said: it is abundant. Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said, commenting on Surah 54, verses 18–22:

Allah the Exalted says, informing about 'Ad, the people of Hud: They also denied their Messenger, just as the people of Nuh had done. And Allah sent upon them ﴿a violent, icy wind﴾, which is the cold, very severe in its chill, ﴿on a day of continuous misfortune﴾, meaning: for them. This was said by al-Dahhak, Qatadah and al-Suddi. ﴿Continuous﴾ means its misfortune and destruction remained upon them, because it was a day on which their worldly punishment was joined to their punishment in the Hereafter.

And His saying: ﴿Uprooting people as if they were trunks of palm trees, hollowed out﴾. This is because the wind would come to one of them, lift him up until it hid him from sight, then turn him upside down onto the top of his head, so he would fall to the ground and it would crush his head, leaving a body without a head. For this reason He said: ﴿As if they were trunks of palm trees, hollowed out. So how was My punishment and My warnings? And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember?﴾

This is an account about Thamud, that they denied their messenger Salih. ﴿So they said: "Shall we follow a single human being from among us? Indeed we would then be in error and madness."﴾ They are saying: "We would have lost and been ruined if we all submitted our leadership to one man from among us!"

Then they wondered at the revelation being cast upon him specifically, to the exclusion of them. Then they accused him of lying, saying: ﴿"Rather, he is a liar, an arrogant one."﴾ That is: one who exceeds the limits of lying. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿"They will know tomorrow who is the arrogant liar."﴾ This is a severe threat to them and a firm warning.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿"Indeed, We are sending the she-camel as a trial for them."﴾ That is, as a test for them. Allah brought forth for them a great, pregnant she-camel from a hard rock, in accordance with what they had asked, to be a proof of Allah against them regarding the truth of Salih, peace be upon him, in what he brought them.

Then He said, commanding His servant and messenger Salih: ﴿"So wait and be patient."﴾ That is: await what their affair will come to, and be patient with them, for the final outcome is yours and victory is yours in this world and the Hereafter. ﴿"And inform them that the water is divided between them."﴾ That is: a day for them and a day for the she-camel, like His saying: ﴿"This is a she-camel; she has a share of water, and you have a share of a known day."﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 155]

* *

His saying: ﴿"Every share of water is attended."﴾ Mujahid said: when she (the camel) was absent, they came to the water, and when she came, they came to the milk.

Then the Exalted said: ﴿"But they called their companion, and he took [the sword] and hamstrung her."﴾ The commentators said: he is the one who hamstrung the she-camel, and his name was Qudar ibn Salif, and he was the most wretched of his people. Like His saying: ﴿"When the most wretched of them set out."﴾ [al-Shams: 12]. ﴿Fa-ta'atha⁠ (he took [the sword])⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠⁠ means: fa-jasar (he dared/ventured).

﴿"Then he hamstrung her. So how was My punishment and My warnings?"﴾ That is: then I punished them. How was My punishment [to them] for their disbelief in Me and their denial of My messenger? ﴿"Indeed, We sent upon them a single blast, and they became like the dry crumbled remains of a fence-builder's enclosure."﴾ That is: they were annihilated to the last one, not one of them remained, and they became silent and perished as dry, withered plants and vegetation wither. This was said by more than one of the commentators. Al-Muhtazir (the fence-builder) — said al-Suddi — is the pasture in the desert when it dries up, scorches, and the wind scatters it.

Ibn Zayd said: the Arabs used to make an enclosure for camels and livestock from dry thorns, and this is what is meant by His saying: ﴿"like the crumbled remains of a fence-builder."﴾

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿"like the crumbled remains of a fence-builder"﴾ refers to the dust scattered from a wall. This is a strange opinion, and the first is stronger, and Allah knows best.

He, exalted is He, informs about the people of Lut: how they denied their Messenger and opposed him, and how they committed the abhorrent act of intercourse with males, an abomination that none of the worlds had committed before them. For this reason, Allah destroyed them with a destruction He had not inflicted on any other nation. He, exalted is He, commanded Jibril (Gabriel) (peace be upon him), who lifted up their cities until he brought them close to the heights of the sky, then overturned them upon them and let them fall, and they were followed by stones of baked clay, layered and piled up. For this reason He says here: ﴿Indeed, We sent upon them a violent wind-borne storm of stones﴾, and the word means stones. ﴿Except the family of Lut; We saved them at dawn﴾, meaning they went out at the end of the night and were saved from what befell their people. None of Lut's people believed in him, not even a single man, not even his wife; what befell her people befell her too. The Prophet of Allah, Lut, went out with his daughters from among them, safe, and no harm touched him. For this reason Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿Thus do We reward those who give thanks. And he had already warned them of Our assault﴾, meaning that before the punishment descended upon them, he had warned them of Allah's might and His punishment, but they paid no heed to that, did not incline to it, and instead doubted it and disputed about it. ﴿And they had already sought to seduce him from his guests﴾. This was the night the angels came to him: Jibril, Mika'il (Michael) and Israfil (Raphael), in the form of beardless, handsome young men, as a trial from Allah for them. Lut hosted them, and his wife, the wicked old woman, sent word to her people and informed them about Lut's guests. They came rushing to him from every direction. Lut closed the door against them, and they began trying to break the door down. This was in the evening, and Lut (peace be upon him) was repelling them and keeping them away from his guests, saying to them: ﴿These are my daughters﴾, meaning their women, ﴿if you are going to act﴾ [Al-Hijr 15:71]. ﴿They said: You already know that we have no claim on your daughters, and you know well what we want﴾ [Hud 11:79], meaning that we have no desire for them. When the situation grew severe and they refused anything but entering, Jibril (peace be upon him) came out to them and struck their eyes with the tip of his wing, and their eyes were obliterated. It is said that their eyes were wiped out from their faces.

It is also said that they were left with no eyes at all, so they turned back, groping along the walls, threatening Lut (peace be upon him), until morning.

Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And in the early morning there came upon them a settled punishment﴾, meaning there was no escape for them from it and no way for them to be free of it. ﴿So taste My punishment and warnings. And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there anyone who will remember?﴾

And he had already warned them of Our assault﴾, meaning that before the punishment descended upon them, he had warned them of Allah's might and His punishment, but they paid no heed to that, did not incline to it, and instead doubted it and disputed about it. ﴿And they had already sought to seduce him from his guests﴾. This was the night the angels came to him: Jibril, Mika'il (Michael) and Israfil (Raphael), in the form of beardless, handsome young men, as a trial from Allah for them. Lut hosted them, and his wife, the wicked old woman, sent word to her people and informed them about Lut's guests. They came rushing to him from every direction. Lut closed the door against them, and they began trying to break the door down. This was in the evening, and Lut (peace be upon him) was repelling them and keeping them away from his guests, saying to them: ﴿These are my daughters﴾, meaning their women, ﴿if you are going to act﴾ [Al-Hijr 15:71]. ﴿They said: You already know that we have no claim on your daughters, and you know well what we want﴾ [Hud 11:79], meaning that we have no desire for them. When the situation grew severe and they refused anything but entering, Jibril (peace be upon him) came out to them and struck their eyes with the tip of his wing, and their eyes were obliterated. It is said that their eyes were wiped out from their faces.

It is also said that they were left with no eyes at all, so they turned back, groping along the walls, threatening Lut (peace be upon him), until morning.

Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿And in the early morning there came upon them a settled punishment﴾, meaning there was no escape for them from it and no way for them to be free of it. ﴿So taste My punishment and warnings. And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there anyone who will remember?﴾

He, exalted is He, informs about the people of Lut: how they denied their Messenger and opposed him, and how they committed the abhorrent act of intercourse with males, an abomination that none of the worlds had committed before them. For this reason, Allah destroyed them with a destruction He had not inflicted on any other nation. He, exalted is He, commanded Jibril (Gabriel) (peace be upon him), who lifted up their cities until he brought them close to the heights of the sky, then overturned them upon them and let them fall, and they were followed by stones of baked clay, layered and piled up. For this reason He says here: ﴿Indeed, We sent upon them a violent wind-borne storm of stones﴾, and the word means stones. ﴿Except the family of Lut; We saved them at dawn﴾, meaning they went out at the end of the night and were saved from what befell their people. He strengthened them both with great miracles and numerous signs, but they denied them all. So Allah seized them with the seizing of the Mighty, the All-Powerful. That is, Allah destroyed them and left of them neither a trace, nor an eye, nor a remnant.

Then He said: ﴿Are your disbelievers better than those?﴾ That is: O polytheists among the disbelievers of Quraysh, are you better than those who were mentioned before, who were destroyed because of their denial of the Messengers and their disbelief in the Scriptures? ﴿Or do you have immunity in the Scriptures?﴾ That is: or do you have from Allah an immunity that no punishment or retribution will reach you?

Then He said, informing about them: ﴿Or do they say, "We are a united body that will be victorious"?﴾ That is: they believe that they support one another, and that their numbers will protect them from whoever intends them harm. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The multitude will be routed and they will turn their backs﴾. That is: their unity will be scattered and they will be defeated.

Al-Bukhari said: Ishaq narrated to us, Khalid narrated to us, from Khalid. And he also said: Muhammad narrated to us, 'Affan ibn Muslim narrated to us, from Wuhayb, from Khalid, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: that the Prophet ﷺ said, while he was in his tent on the day of Badr: "I beseech You by Your covenant and Your promise. O Allah, if You will, You will not be worshipped after this day, ever." Then Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, took his hand and said: "That is enough for you, O Messenger of Allah! You have pressed your Lord insistently." He came out leaping in his armour, saying: ﴿The multitude will be routed and they will turn their backs. Rather, the Hour is their appointed time, and the Hour is more calamitous and bitter.﴾

This was also narrated by al-Bukhari and an-Nasa'i in various places, from the hadith of Khalid, who is Mihran al-Hadhdha', with the same chain. [Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. (2915, 3953, 4875, 4877) and an-Nasa'i in as-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (11557).]

Allah informs us, may He be exalted, that the criminals are in error concerning the truth and in a "sa'ar" (blaze, turmoil) of the doubts and confusion in their opinions. This applies to everyone who is characterized by that, whether a disbeliever or an innovator (mubtadi') from among all the sects.

Then He said: ﴿On the Day they are dragged into the Fire on their faces﴾, meaning: just as they were in turmoil, doubt and hesitation, which led them to the Fire, and just as they were astray, they will be dragged into it on their faces, not knowing where they are going. And it will be said to them, as rebuke and reproach: ﴿Taste the touch of Saqar﴾.

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, all things We have created with qadar (divine decree)﴾, like His saying: ﴿And He created everything and determined it with precise determination﴾ [al-Furqan: 2], and His saying: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, who created and proportioned, and who determined and guided﴾ [al-A'la: 1–3], meaning: He decreed a decree, and guided the creatures to it. For this reason, the Imams of the Sunnah use this noble verse to establish the qadar of Allah that precedes His creation, which is His knowledge of things before they exist and His writing of them before they come into being. They refuted, by this verse and what resembles it of verses, and by the authentic hadiths that have come with its meaning, the sect of the Qadariyyah (those who deny divine decree), who emerged at the end of the era of the Companions. We have discussed this matter in detail, and the hadiths related to it, in the explanation of the "Book of Faith" in the Sahih of al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him. Here we will mention the hadiths related to this noble verse:

Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn Isma'il al-Sahmi, from Muhammad ibn 'Abbad ibn Ja'far, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The polytheists of Quraysh came to the Prophet (ﷺ) disputing with him about qadar, and this was revealed: ﴿On the Day they are dragged into the Fire on their faces: Taste the touch of Saqar. Indeed, all things We have created with qadar﴾.

It was also narrated in this way by Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, from the hadith of Waki', from Sufyan al-Thawri, with the same chain [[al-Musnad (2/444), Sahih Muslim no. (2656), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3290), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (83).]].

Al-Bazzar said: Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad narrated to us, Yunus ibn al-Harith narrated to us, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: These verses were not revealed except concerning the people of qadar: ﴿Indeed, the criminals are in error and turmoil. On the Day they are dragged into the Fire on their faces: Taste the touch of Saqar. Indeed, all things We have created with qadar﴾ [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (2265), Kashf al-Astar. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/117): "In it is Yunus ibn al-Harith, whom Ibn Ma'in and Ibn Hibban declared reliable, but there is some weakness in him, and the rest of its narrators are reliable."]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Sahl ibn Salih al-Antaki narrated to us, Qurrah ibn Habib narrated to me, from Kinanah: Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Amr ibn Ja'dah, from Ibn Zurarah, from his father, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he recited this verse: ﴿Taste the touch of Saqar. Indeed, all things We have created with qadar﴾, and said: "It was revealed concerning some people from my Ummah who will be in the last age, who will deny the qadar of Allah" [[Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (5/276) through the route of Qurrah ibn Habib from Jarir ibn Hazim — I suspect that Kinanah has dropped out from it — from Sa'id ibn Amr with the same.]].

Al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah narrated to us, Marwan ibn Shuja' al-Jazari narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, who said: I came to Ibn 'Abbas while he was drawing water from Zamzam, and the lower parts of his garments were wet. I said to him: "Qadar has been spoken about." He said: "Have they really done it?" I said: "Yes." He said: "By Allah, this verse was revealed only concerning them: ﴿Taste the touch of Saqar. Indeed, all things We have created with qadar﴾. They are the worst of this Ummah. Do not visit their sick, and do not pray over their dead. If I see any one of them, I will gouge out his eyes with these two fingers of mine."

Ahmad also narrated it by another route, in which there is a marfu' (directly traced to the Prophet) report. He said:

Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us, al-Awza'i narrated to us, from some of his brothers, from Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd al-Makki, from Abdullah ibn 'Abbas, who said: It was said to him: "A man has come to us who denies qadar." He said: "Point him out to me," and he was blind. They said: "What will you do with him, O Abu 'Abbas?" He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, if I gain power over him I will bite his nose until I cut it off, and if his neck comes into my hand I will break it, for I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'As if I see the women of Banu Fihr circumambulating al-Khazraj, their buttocks shaking, polytheists. This is the first shirk of this Ummah. By Him in whose hand is my soul, the evil of their opinions will certainly lead them until they remove Allah from having decreed good, just as they removed Him from having decreed evil.'" [[al-Musnad (1/330).]]

Then Ahmad narrated it from Abu al-Mughirah, from al-Awza'i, from al-Ala' ibn al-Hajjaj, from Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd, and mentioned the like of it [[al-Musnad (1/330).]]. They did not take it out (i.e., the compilers of the six books did not record it).

Ahmad said: Abdullah ibn Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub narrated to us, Abu Sakhr narrated to me, from Nafi', who said: Ibn 'Umar had a friend from the people of Syria who used to correspond with him. Abdullah ibn 'Umar wrote to him: "It has reached me that you have spoken about something of qadar. Beware of writing to me, for I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'There will be among my Ummah people who deny qadar.'"

Abu Dawud narrated it from Ahmad ibn Hanbal, with the same [[al-Musnad (2/90) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4613).]].

Ahmad said: Anas ibn 'Iyad narrated to us, Umar ibn Abdullah, mawla of Ghufrah, narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every nation has its Magians, and the Magians of my Ummah are those who say: 'There is no qadar. If they fall sick, do not visit them, and if they die, do not attend their funerals.'" [[al-Musnad (2/86).]]

No one from among the authors of the six books recorded it through this route.

Ahmad said: Qutaybah narrated to us, Rishdin narrated to us, from Abu Sakhr Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "There will be in this Ummah a transformation (maskh). Beware, it will be among those who deny qadar and the zindiqiyyah (heretics)."

It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, from the hadith of Abu Sakhr Humayd ibn Ziyad, with the same. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih gharib" [[al-Musnad (2/108), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2152), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4061).]].

Ahmad said: Ishaq ibn al-Tabba' narrated to us, Malik informed me, from Ziyad ibn Sa'd, from Amr ibn Muslim, from Tawus al-Yamani, who said: I heard Ibn 'Umar say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Everything is by qadar, even incapacity and cleverness."

Muslim narrated it alone, from the hadith of Malik [[al-Musnad (2/110), Sahih Muslim no. (2655).]].

In the authentic hadith: "Seek help from Allah and do not be incapable. If something befalls you, say: 'Allah decreed, and He does what He wills.' Do not say: 'If only I had done such-and-such, it would have been so,' for 'if only' opens the work of Satan" [[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih no. (2664) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

And in the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Know that if the whole Ummah gathered to benefit you with something that Allah had not written for you, they would not benefit you; and if they gathered to harm you with something that Allah had not written against you, they would not harm you. The pens have dried and the scrolls have been folded" [[Narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad (1/293).]].

Ahmad said: al-Hasan ibn Sawwar narrated to us, al-Layth narrated to us, from Mu'awiyah, from Ayyub ibn Ziyad, Ubadah ibn al-Walid ibn Ubadah narrated to me, my father narrated to me, saying: I entered upon Ubadah while he was ill, and I thought he was near death. I said: "O father, advise me and strive for me." He said: "Seat me up." When they seated him, he said: "O my son, you will not taste the taste of faith, nor reach the true reality of knowledge of Allah, until you believe in qadar, its good and its evil." I said: "O father, how can I know what the good and evil of qadar is?" He said: "You know that what missed you would not have hit you, and what hit you would not have missed you. O my son, I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The first thing Allah created was the pen. Then He said to it: Write. So it flowed in that very hour with what will exist until the Day of Resurrection.'" O my son, if you die not upon this, you will enter the Fire [[al-Musnad (5/317).]].

al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Yahya ibn Musa al-Balkhi, from Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, from Abd al-Wahid ibn Sulaym, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from al-Walid ibn Ubadah, from his father, with the same. He said: "Hasan sahih gharib" [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3319).]].

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Mansur, from Rib'i ibn Khirash, from a man, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A servant does not believe until he believes in four things: he testifies that there is no god but Allah, and that I am the Messenger of Allah, whom He sent with the truth; and he believes in death, and he believes in resurrection after death, and he believes in qadar, its good and its evil."

Likewise al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of al-Nadr ibn Shumayl, from Shu'bah, from Mansur, with the same [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2145), and Ahmad in his Musnad (1/133) from Waki', and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak (1/33) from Abu Hudhayfah, both from Sufyan al-Thawri with the same. Al-Daraqutni in al-'Ilal (3/196) preferred this version, saying: "The hadith of Shurayk, Waraqa, Jarir and Amr ibn Abi Qays, from Mansur, from Rib'i, from Ali. Sufyan al-Thawri, Za'idah Abu al-Ahwas and Sulayman al-Taymi differed from them and narrated it from Mansur, from Rib'i, from a man of Banu Rashid, from Ali, and this is the correct version."]]. He also narrated it from the hadith of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, from Shu'bah, from Mansur, from Rib'i, from Ali, and mentioned it, and said: "This, in my view, is more sound." Likewise Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Shurayk, from Mansur, from Rib'i, from Ali, with the same [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2145) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (81).]].

It is established in Sahih Muslim, from the narration of Abdullah ibn Wahb and others, from Abu Hani al-Khawlani, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli, from Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah wrote the decrees of the creatures fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth." Ibn Wahb added: ﴿and His Throne was upon the water﴾ [Hud: 7]. al-Tirmidhi narrated it and said: "Hasan sahih gharib" [[Sahih Muslim no. (2653), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2156).]].

* *

His saying: ﴿And Our command is but one, like a glance of the eye﴾. This is an information about the execution of His will in His creation, just as He informed of the execution of His decree among them. So He said: ﴿And Our command is but one﴾, meaning: We only command a thing once, without needing to repeat it a second time, so that what We command comes into existence immediately, ﴿like a glance of the eye﴾, without delaying even a blink. How excellent is what one of the poets said:

When Allah wills a matter, He only says to it: "Be," and it is.

* *

His saying: ﴿And We have already destroyed your likes﴾, meaning: your counterparts and your predecessors among the earlier nations who denied the messengers. ﴿So is there any who will remember?﴾, meaning: is there anyone who will take heed from what Allah humiliated those people with, and the punishment He decreed for them? As He said: ﴿And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire, as was done to their likes before﴾ [Saba': 54].

* *

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 54, verses 47–55 (part 2 of 2):

Regarding His words, ﴿And everything they did is in the Zubur﴾, meaning it is written against them in the books that are in the hands of the angels, peace be upon them. ﴿And every small and great thing﴾, meaning from their deeds, ﴿is inscribed﴾, meaning gathered against them and written in their records. Nothing small or great is left out without being counted.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu 'Amir narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Muslim ibn Banak narrated to us: I heard 'Amir ibn 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr say, 'Awf ibn al-Harith narrated to me, and he is the nephew of 'A'isha through her mother, from 'A'isha, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "O 'A'isha, beware of the trivial sins, for they have a seeker from Allah."

An-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah also narrated it through the route of Sa'id ibn Muslim ibn Banak al-Madani.[[Al-Musnad (6/151) and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (4243).]] Ahmad, Ibn Ma'in, Abu Hatim, and others declared him trustworthy (thiqah).

The Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir also narrated it in the biography of this Sa'id ibn Muslim through another route.[[Tarikh Dimashq (7/353, manuscript), through the route of Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi and al-Qa'nabi, both from Sa'id ibn Muslim.]] Then Sa'id said: I narrated this hadith to 'Amir ibn Hisham, and he said to me: "Woe to you, O Sa'id ibn Muslim! Sulayman ibn al-Mughira narrated to me that he committed a sin and considered it small, and someone came to him in his dream and said to him: 'O Sulayman:'

Do not belittle any small sin,
For the small one, tomorrow, will become great.
Indeed, the small, even if its time has long passed,
Is inscribed by God as an inscription.
So restrain your desire from idleness, and do not be
Hard to lead, and exert yourself in exertion.
Indeed, the lover, when he loves his God,
The heart takes flight and is inspired to reflect.
So ask your God for guidance with sincere intention,
For your Lord is sufficient as a guide and a helper.[[Tarikh Dimashq (7/353, manuscript section).]]

Regarding His words, ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and rivers﴾, meaning, in contrast to the wretched, who are in misguidance, madness, and being dragged on their faces into the Fire, along with reproach, rebuke, and threat.

* *

Regarding His words, ﴿In a seat of truth﴾, meaning in the abode of Allah's honour, His good pleasure, His bounty, His kindness, His generosity, and His favour, ﴿in the presence of a Sovereign, All-Powerful﴾, meaning in the presence of the Great King, the Creator of all things and their Determiner, who is Able to do whatever He wills of what they seek and desire. Imam Ahmad said:

Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Amr ibn Aws, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who traced it to the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Those who act justly are with Allah on the Day of Resurrection, upon pulpits of light, on the right hand of the Most Merciful, and both His hands are right: those who are just in their rule, in their families, and in what they are entrusted with."

Muslim and an-Nasa'i alone narrated it, from the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna, with its chain similarly.[[Sahih Muslim, no. (1827), and Sunan an-Nasa'i (8/221).]]

End of the tafsir of Surah "Iqtarabat" (Al-Qamar). All praise and grace belong to Allah, and success and protection are from Him.

Allah informs us, may He be exalted, that the criminals are in error concerning the truth and in a "sa'ar" (blaze, turmoil) of the doubts and confusion in their opinions. This applies to everyone who is characterized by that, whether a disbeliever or an innovator (mubtadi') from among all the sects.

Then He said: ﴿On the Day they are dragged into the Fire on their faces﴾, meaning: just as they were in turmoil, doubt and hesitation, which led them to the Fire, and just as they were astray, they will be dragged into it on their faces, not knowing where they are going. And it will be said to them, as rebuke and reproach: ﴿Taste the touch of Saqar﴾.

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, all things We have created with qadar (divine decree)﴾, like His saying: ﴿And He created everything and determined it with precise determination﴾ [al-Furqan: 2], and His saying: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, who created and proportioned, and who determined and guided﴾ [al-A'la: 1–3], meaning: He decreed a decree, and guided the creatures to it. For this reason, the Imams of the Sunnah use this noble verse to establish the qadar of Allah that precedes His creation, which is His knowledge of things before they exist and His writing of them before they come into being. They refuted, by this verse and what resembles it of verses, and by the authentic hadiths that have come with its meaning, the sect of the Qadariyyah (those who deny divine decree), who emerged at the end of the era of the Companions. We have discussed this matter in detail, and the hadiths related to it, in the explanation of the "Book of Faith" in the Sahih of al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him. Here we will mention the hadiths related to this noble verse:

Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn Isma'il al-Sahmi, from Muhammad ibn 'Abbad ibn Ja'far, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The polytheists of Quraysh came to the Prophet (ﷺ) disputing with him about qadar, and this was revealed: ﴿On the Day they are dragged into the Fire on their faces: Taste the touch of Saqar. Indeed, all things We have created with qadar﴾.

It was also narrated in this way by Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, from the hadith of Waki', from Sufyan al-Thawri, with the same chain [[al-Musnad (2/444), Sahih Muslim no. (2656), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3290), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (83).]].

Al-Bazzar said: Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad narrated to us, Yunus ibn al-Harith narrated to us, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: These verses were not revealed except concerning the people of qadar: ﴿Indeed, the criminals are in error and turmoil. On the Day they are dragged into the Fire on their faces: Taste the touch of Saqar. Indeed, all things We have created with qadar﴾ [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (2265), Kashf al-Astar. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/117): "In it is Yunus ibn al-Harith, whom Ibn Ma'in and Ibn Hibban declared reliable, but there is some weakness in him, and the rest of its narrators are reliable."]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Sahl ibn Salih al-Antaki narrated to us, Qurrah ibn Habib narrated to me, from Kinanah: Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Amr ibn Ja'dah, from Ibn Zurarah, from his father, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he recited this verse: ﴿Taste the touch of Saqar. Indeed, all things We have created with qadar﴾, and said: "It was revealed concerning some people from my Ummah who will be in the last age, who will deny the qadar of Allah" [[Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (5/276) through the route of Qurrah ibn Habib from Jarir ibn Hazim — I suspect that Kinanah has dropped out from it — from Sa'id ibn Amr with the same.]].

Al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah narrated to us, Marwan ibn Shuja' al-Jazari narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, who said: I came to Ibn 'Abbas while he was drawing water from Zamzam, and the lower parts of his garments were wet. I said to him: "Qadar has been spoken about." He said: "Have they really done it?" I said: "Yes." He said: "By Allah, this verse was revealed only concerning them: ﴿Taste the touch of Saqar. Indeed, all things We have created with qadar﴾. They are the worst of this Ummah. Do not visit their sick, and do not pray over their dead. If I see any one of them, I will gouge out his eyes with these two fingers of mine."

Ahmad also narrated it by another route, in which there is a marfu' (directly traced to the Prophet) report. He said:

Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us, al-Awza'i narrated to us, from some of his brothers, from Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd al-Makki, from Abdullah ibn 'Abbas, who said: It was said to him: "A man has come to us who denies qadar." He said: "Point him out to me," and he was blind. They said: "What will you do with him, O Abu 'Abbas?" He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, if I gain power over him I will bite his nose until I cut it off, and if his neck comes into my hand I will break it, for I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'As if I see the women of Banu Fihr circumambulating al-Khazraj, their buttocks shaking, polytheists. This is the first shirk of this Ummah. By Him in whose hand is my soul, the evil of their opinions will certainly lead them until they remove Allah from having decreed good, just as they removed Him from having decreed evil.'" [[al-Musnad (1/330).]]

Then Ahmad narrated it from Abu al-Mughirah, from al-Awza'i, from al-Ala' ibn al-Hajjaj, from Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd, and mentioned the like of it [[al-Musnad (1/330).]]. They did not take it out (i.e., the compilers of the six books did not record it).

Ahmad said: Abdullah ibn Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub narrated to us, Abu Sakhr narrated to me, from Nafi', who said: Ibn 'Umar had a friend from the people of Syria who used to correspond with him. Abdullah ibn 'Umar wrote to him: "It has reached me that you have spoken about something of qadar. Beware of writing to me, for I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'There will be among my Ummah people who deny qadar.'"

Abu Dawud narrated it from Ahmad ibn Hanbal, with the same [[al-Musnad (2/90) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4613).]].

Ahmad said: Anas ibn 'Iyad narrated to us, Umar ibn Abdullah, mawla of Ghufrah, narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every nation has its Magians, and the Magians of my Ummah are those who say: 'There is no qadar. If they fall sick, do not visit them, and if they die, do not attend their funerals.'" [[al-Musnad (2/86).]]

No one from among the authors of the six books recorded it through this route.

Ahmad said: Qutaybah narrated to us, Rishdin narrated to us, from Abu Sakhr Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "There will be in this Ummah a transformation (maskh). Beware, it will be among those who deny qadar and the zindiqiyyah (heretics)."

It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, from the hadith of Abu Sakhr Humayd ibn Ziyad, with the same. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih gharib" [[al-Musnad (2/108), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2152), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4061).]].

Ahmad said: Ishaq ibn al-Tabba' narrated to us, Malik informed me, from Ziyad ibn Sa'd, from Amr ibn Muslim, from Tawus al-Yamani, who said: I heard Ibn 'Umar say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Everything is by qadar, even incapacity and cleverness."

Muslim narrated it alone, from the hadith of Malik [[al-Musnad (2/110), Sahih Muslim no. (2655).]].

In the authentic hadith: "Seek help from Allah and do not be incapable. If something befalls you, say: 'Allah decreed, and He does what He wills.' Do not say: 'If only I had done such-and-such, it would have been so,' for 'if only' opens the work of Satan" [[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih no. (2664) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

And in the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Know that if the whole Ummah gathered to benefit you with something that Allah had not written for you, they would not benefit you; and if they gathered to harm you with something that Allah had not written against you, they would not harm you. The pens have dried and the scrolls have been folded" [[Narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad (1/293).]].

Ahmad said: al-Hasan ibn Sawwar narrated to us, al-Layth narrated to us, from Mu'awiyah, from Ayyub ibn Ziyad, Ubadah ibn al-Walid ibn Ubadah narrated to me, my father narrated to me, saying: I entered upon Ubadah while he was ill, and I thought he was near death. I said: "O father, advise me and strive for me." He said: "Seat me up." When they seated him, he said: "O my son, you will not taste the taste of faith, nor reach the true reality of knowledge of Allah, until you believe in qadar, its good and its evil." I said: "O father, how can I know what the good and evil of qadar is?" He said: "You know that what missed you would not have hit you, and what hit you would not have missed you. O my son, I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The first thing Allah created was the pen. Then He said to it: Write. So it flowed in that very hour with what will exist until the Day of Resurrection.'" O my son, if you die not upon this, you will enter the Fire [[al-Musnad (5/317).]].

al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Yahya ibn Musa al-Balkhi, from Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, from Abd al-Wahid ibn Sulaym, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from al-Walid ibn Ubadah, from his father, with the same. He said: "Hasan sahih gharib" [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3319).]].

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Mansur, from Rib'i ibn Khirash, from a man, from Ali ibn Abi Talib, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "A servant does not believe until he believes in four things: he testifies that there is no god but Allah, and that I am the Messenger of Allah, whom He sent with the truth; and he believes in death, and he believes in resurrection after death, and he believes in qadar, its good and its evil."

Likewise al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of al-Nadr ibn Shumayl, from Shu'bah, from Mansur, with the same [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2145), and Ahmad in his Musnad (1/133) from Waki', and al-Hakim in his Mustadrak (1/33) from Abu Hudhayfah, both from Sufyan al-Thawri with the same. Al-Daraqutni in al-'Ilal (3/196) preferred this version, saying: "The hadith of Shurayk, Waraqa, Jarir and Amr ibn Abi Qays, from Mansur, from Rib'i, from Ali. Sufyan al-Thawri, Za'idah Abu al-Ahwas and Sulayman al-Taymi differed from them and narrated it from Mansur, from Rib'i, from a man of Banu Rashid, from Ali, and this is the correct version."]]. He also narrated it from the hadith of Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, from Shu'bah, from Mansur, from Rib'i, from Ali, and mentioned it, and said: "This, in my view, is more sound." Likewise Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Shurayk, from Mansur, from Rib'i, from Ali, with the same [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2145) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (81).]].

It is established in Sahih Muslim, from the narration of Abdullah ibn Wahb and others, from Abu Hani al-Khawlani, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Hubuli, from Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah wrote the decrees of the creatures fifty thousand years before He created the heavens and the earth." Ibn Wahb added: ﴿and His Throne was upon the water﴾ [Hud: 7]. al-Tirmidhi narrated it and said: "Hasan sahih gharib" [[Sahih Muslim no. (2653), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2156).]].

* *

His saying: ﴿And Our command is but one, like a glance of the eye﴾. This is an information about the execution of His will in His creation, just as He informed of the execution of His decree among them. So He said: ﴿And Our command is but one﴾, meaning: We only command a thing once, without needing to repeat it a second time, so that what We command comes into existence immediately, ﴿like a glance of the eye﴾, without delaying even a blink. How excellent is what one of the poets said:

When Allah wills a matter, He only says to it: "Be," and it is.

* *

His saying: ﴿And We have already destroyed your likes﴾, meaning: your counterparts and your predecessors among the earlier nations who denied the messengers. ﴿So is there any who will remember?﴾, meaning: is there anyone who will take heed from what Allah humiliated those people with, and the punishment He decreed for them? As He said: ﴿And a barrier will be placed between them and what they desire, as was done to their likes before﴾ [Saba': 54].

* *

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 54, verses 47–55 (part 2 of 2):

Regarding His words, ﴿And everything they did is in the Zubur﴾, meaning it is written against them in the books that are in the hands of the angels, peace be upon them. ﴿And every small and great thing﴾, meaning from their deeds, ﴿is inscribed﴾, meaning gathered against them and written in their records. Nothing small or great is left out without being counted.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu 'Amir narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Muslim ibn Banak narrated to us: I heard 'Amir ibn 'Abdullah ibn al-Zubayr say, 'Awf ibn al-Harith narrated to me, and he is the nephew of 'A'isha through her mother, from 'A'isha, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "O 'A'isha, beware of the trivial sins, for they have a seeker from Allah."

An-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah also narrated it through the route of Sa'id ibn Muslim ibn Banak al-Madani.[[Al-Musnad (6/151) and Sunan Ibn Majah, no. (4243).]] Ahmad, Ibn Ma'in, Abu Hatim, and others declared him trustworthy (thiqah).

The Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir also narrated it in the biography of this Sa'id ibn Muslim through another route.[[Tarikh Dimashq (7/353, manuscript), through the route of Abu 'Amir al-'Aqadi and al-Qa'nabi, both from Sa'id ibn Muslim.]] Then Sa'id said: I narrated this hadith to 'Amir ibn Hisham, and he said to me: "Woe to you, O Sa'id ibn Muslim! Sulayman ibn al-Mughira narrated to me that he committed a sin and considered it small, and someone came to him in his dream and said to him: 'O Sulayman:'

Do not belittle any small sin,
For the small one, tomorrow, will become great.
Indeed, the small, even if its time has long passed,
Is inscribed by God as an inscription.
So restrain your desire from idleness, and do not be
Hard to lead, and exert yourself in exertion.
Indeed, the lover, when he loves his God,
The heart takes flight and is inspired to reflect.
So ask your God for guidance with sincere intention,
For your Lord is sufficient as a guide and a helper.[[Tarikh Dimashq (7/353, manuscript section).]]

Regarding His words, ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and rivers﴾, meaning, in contrast to the wretched, who are in misguidance, madness, and being dragged on their faces into the Fire, along with reproach, rebuke, and threat.

* *

Regarding His words, ﴿In a seat of truth﴾, meaning in the abode of Allah's honour, His good pleasure, His bounty, His kindness, His generosity, and His favour, ﴿in the presence of a Sovereign, All-Powerful﴾, meaning in the presence of the Great King, the Creator of all things and their Determiner, who is Able to do whatever He wills of what they seek and desire. Imam Ahmad said:

Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Amr ibn Aws, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who traced it to the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "Those who act justly are with Allah on the Day of Resurrection, upon pulpits of light, on the right hand of the Most Merciful, and both His hands are right: those who are just in their rule, in their families, and in what they are entrusted with."

Muslim and an-Nasa'i alone narrated it, from the hadith of Sufyan ibn 'Uyayna, with its chain similarly.[[Sahih Muslim, no. (1827), and Sunan an-Nasa'i (8/221).]]

End of the tafsir of Surah "Iqtarabat" (Al-Qamar). All praise and grace belong to Allah, and success and protection are from Him.

Allah informs us, may He be exalted, that the criminals are in error concerning the truth and in a "sa'ar" (blaze, turmoil) of the doubts and confusion in their opinions. This applies to everyone who is characterized by that, whether a disbeliever or an innovator (mubtadi') from among all the sects.

Then He said: ﴿On the Day they are dragged into the Fire on their faces﴾, meaning: just as they were in turmoil, doubt and hesitation, which led them to the Fire, and just as they were astray, they will be dragged into it on their faces, not knowing where they are going. And it will be said to them, as rebuke and reproach: ﴿Taste the touch of Saqar﴾.

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed, all things We have created with qadar (divine decree)﴾, like His saying: ﴿And He created everything and determined it with precise determination﴾ [al-Furqan: 2], and His saying: ﴿Glorify the name of your Lord, the Most High, who created and proportioned, and who determined and guided﴾ [al-A'la: 1–3], meaning: He decreed a decree, and guided the creatures to it. For this reason, the Imams of the Sunnah use this noble verse to establish the qadar of Allah that precedes His creation, which is His knowledge of things before they exist and His writing of them before they come into being. They refuted, by this verse and what resembles it of verses, and by the authentic hadiths that have come with its meaning, the sect of the Qadariyyah (those who deny divine decree), who emerged at the end of the era of the Companions. We have discussed this matter in detail, and the hadiths related to it, in the explanation of the "Book of Faith" in the Sahih of al-Bukhari, may Allah have mercy on him. Here we will mention the hadiths related to this noble verse:

Ahmad said: Waki' narrated to us, Sufyan al-Thawri narrated to us, from Ziyad ibn Isma'il al-Sahmi, from Muhammad ibn 'Abbad ibn Ja'far, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The polytheists of Quraysh came to the Prophet (ﷺ) disputing with him about qadar, and this was revealed: ﴿On the Day they are dragged into the Fire on their faces: Taste the touch of Saqar. Indeed, all things We have created with qadar﴾.

It was also narrated in this way by Muslim, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, from the hadith of Waki', from Sufyan al-Thawri, with the same chain [[al-Musnad (2/444), Sahih Muslim no. (2656), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3290), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (83).]].

Al-Bazzar said: Amr ibn 'Ali narrated to us, al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad narrated to us, Yunus ibn al-Harith narrated to us, from Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: These verses were not revealed except concerning the people of qadar: ﴿Indeed, the criminals are in error and turmoil. On the Day they are dragged into the Fire on their faces: Taste the touch of Saqar. Indeed, all things We have created with qadar﴾ [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (2265), Kashf al-Astar. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/117): "In it is Yunus ibn al-Harith, whom Ibn Ma'in and Ibn Hibban declared reliable, but there is some weakness in him, and the rest of its narrators are reliable."]].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Sahl ibn Salih al-Antaki narrated to us, Qurrah ibn Habib narrated to me, from Kinanah: Jarir ibn Hazim narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Amr ibn Ja'dah, from Ibn Zurarah, from his father, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he recited this verse: ﴿Taste the touch of Saqar. Indeed, all things We have created with qadar﴾, and said: "It was revealed concerning some people from my Ummah who will be in the last age, who will deny the qadar of Allah" [[Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (5/276) through the route of Qurrah ibn Habib from Jarir ibn Hazim — I suspect that Kinanah has dropped out from it — from Sa'id ibn Amr with the same.]].

Al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah narrated to us, Marwan ibn Shuja' al-Jazari narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik ibn Jurayj, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, who said: I came to Ibn 'Abbas while he was drawing water from Zamzam, and the lower parts of his garments were wet. I said to him: "Qadar has been spoken about." He said: "Have they really done it?" I said: "Yes." He said: "By Allah, this verse was revealed only concerning them: ﴿Taste the touch of Saqar. Indeed, all things We have created with qadar﴾. They are the worst of this Ummah. Do not visit their sick, and do not pray over their dead. If I see any one of them, I will gouge out his eyes with these two fingers of mine."

Ahmad also narrated it by another route, in which there is a marfu' (directly traced to the Prophet) report. He said:

Abu al-Mughirah narrated to us, al-Awza'i narrated to us, from some of his brothers, from Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd al-Makki, from Abdullah ibn 'Abbas, who said: It was said to him: "A man has come to us who denies qadar." He said: "Point him out to me," and he was blind. They said: "What will you do with him, O Abu 'Abbas?" He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, if I gain power over him I will bite his nose until I cut it off, and if his neck comes into my hand I will break it, for I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'As if I see the women of Banu Fihr circumambulating al-Khazraj, their buttocks shaking, polytheists. This is the first shirk of this Ummah. By Him in whose hand is my soul, the evil of their opinions will certainly lead them until they remove Allah from having decreed good, just as they removed Him from having decreed evil.'" [[al-Musnad (1/330).]]

Then Ahmad narrated it from Abu al-Mughirah, from al-Awza'i, from al-Ala' ibn al-Hajjaj, from Muhammad ibn 'Ubayd, and mentioned the like of it [[al-Musnad (1/330).]]. They did not take it out (i.e., the compilers of the six books did not record it).

Ahmad said: Abdullah ibn Yazid narrated to us, Sa'id ibn Abi Ayyub narrated to us, Abu Sakhr narrated to me, from Nafi', who said: Ibn 'Umar had a friend from the people of Syria who used to correspond with him. Abdullah ibn 'Umar wrote to him: "It has reached me that you have spoken about something of qadar. Beware of writing to me, for I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'There will be among my Ummah people who deny qadar.'"

Abu Dawud narrated it from Ahmad ibn Hanbal, with the same [[al-Musnad (2/90) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4613).]].

Ahmad said: Anas ibn 'Iyad narrated to us, Umar ibn Abdullah, mawla of Ghufrah, narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn 'Umar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Every nation has its Magians, and the Magians of my Ummah are those who say: 'There is no qadar. If they fall sick, do not visit them, and if they die, do not attend their funerals.'" [[al-Musnad (2/86).]]

No one from among the authors of the six books recorded it through this route.

Ahmad said: Qutaybah narrated to us, Rishdin narrated to us, from Abu Sakhr Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "There will be in this Ummah a transformation (maskh). Beware, it will be among those who deny qadar and the zindiqiyyah (heretics)."

It was also narrated by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah, from the hadith of Abu Sakhr Humayd ibn Ziyad, with the same. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih gharib" [[al-Musnad (2/108), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2152), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (4061).]].

Ahmad said: Ishaq ibn al-Tabba' narrated to us, Malik informed me, from Ziyad ibn Sa'd, from Amr ibn Muslim, from Tawus al-Yamani, who said: I heard Ibn 'Umar say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Everything is by qadar, even incapacity and cleverness."

Muslim narrated it alone, from the hadith of Malik [[al-Musnad (2/110), Sahih Muslim no. (2655).]].

In the authentic hadith: "Seek help from Allah and do not be incapable. If something befalls you, say: 'Allah decreed, and He does what He wills.' Do not say: 'If only I had done such-and-such, it would have been so,' for 'if only' opens the work of Satan" [[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih no. (2664) from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

And in the hadith of Ibn 'Abbas: the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "Know that if the whole Ummah gathered to benefit you with something that Allah had not written for you, they would not benefit you; and if they gathered to harm you with something that Allah had not written against you, they would not harm you. The pens have dried and the scrolls have been folded" [[Narrated by Imam Ahmad in his Musnad (1/293).]].

Ahmad said: al-Hasan ibn Sawwar narrated to us, al-Layth narrated to us, from Mu'awiyah, from Ayyub ibn Ziyad, Ubadah ibn al-Walid ibn Ubadah narrated to me, my father narrated to me, saying: I entered upon Ubadah while he was ill, and I thought he was near death. I said: "O father, advise me and strive for me." He said: "Seat me up." When they seated him, he said: "O my son, you will not taste the taste of faith, nor reach the true reality of knowledge of Allah, until you believe in qadar, its good and its evil." I said: "O father, how can I know what the good and evil of qadar is?" He said: "You know that what missed you would not have hit you, and what hit you would not have missed you. O my son, I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: 'The first thing Allah created was the pen. Then He said to it: Write. So it flowed in that very hour with what will exist until the Day of Resurrection.'" O my son, if you die not upon this, you will enter the Fire [[al-Musnad (5/317).]].

al-Tirmidhi narrated it from Yahya ibn Musa al-Balkhi, from Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, from Abd al-Wahid ibn Sulaym, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from al-Walid ibn Ubadah, from his father, with the same. He said: "Hasan sahih gharib" [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3319).]].
